You can use this spreadsheet to compute your cost of capital. You can either use the built-in data to compute key inputs (beta, equity risk premium, default spread) or enter them directly. If you choose to use the built in ERP data, you can update the ERP numbers to reflect a more current mature market premuum (since the spreadsheet uses the start of the year numbers).
Estimation of Current Cost of Capital

There are four ways in whch you can estimate your cost of capital. In the first, you can directly input a cost of captial. In the second, you can work through your company's cost of capital inputs in detail, entering business, geogaphical mix and debt, and I will help you estimate a cost of capital. In the third, you can look up the cost of capital for the industry or industries your firm belongs to and in the fourth, you can use a crosssectional distribution  of costs of capital for companies at the start of the year to make your estimate.

The last two rows in each of country/region risk premium tables is set aside for your input to provide you with flexibility to enter some numbers directly. For instance, assume that you have a company that breaks its revenues down into three countries and then puts the rest into "Rest of the World". You can enter the "Rest of the World" in one of these two rows and enter an equity risk premium for the rest of the world. The easiest way to do that is to go into the country equity risk premium worksheet and change the GDP for the three countries that you have data for to zero and compute the global weighted average ERP for the remaining countries. With the regional worksheet, you can use the last two rows to enter the data for an individual country (usually the domestic country) that might be broken out though the rest of the revenues are broken down by region. You can look up the ERP for the country in the country ERP worksheet.

Valuation output!B20.label: PV of Discrete Cash Flows (Yr 1–10)
Valuation output!B20.methodology: Damodaran uses a 10-year discrete forecast period for exponential growth tech companies before assuming mature stable growth. This cell sums the annual Free Cash Flows to the Firm (FCFF) discounted at the time-varying cost of capital from Year 1 through Year 10.
Valuation output!B20.economic_intuition: Early-stage AI companies experience extreme hyper-growth and massive negative cash flows before reaching profitability. A standard 5-year model is too short to capture the transition from cash-burning GPU cluster ramp to high-margin inference software monetization.

Valuation output!B19.label: PV of Terminal Value
Valuation output!B19.methodology: Discounts the Terminal Value ($3,459.5B) calculated in Year 10 back to present value using the cumulative 10-year discount factor (0.4014).
Valuation output!B19.economic_intuition: Represents 80.7% of Anthropic's total going-concern operating assets. In high-growth platform tech, the vast majority of economic value resides in the terminal steady-state cash generation rather than early transition years.

Valuation output!B18.label: Terminal Value in Year 10
Valuation output!B18.methodology: Applies the Gordon Growth Model perpetuity formula: TV = Terminal Cash Flow / (Terminal Cost of Capital - Terminal Growth Rate). Terminal growth is constrained to the 10-year risk-free rate of 4.90% to prevent the company from mathematically outgrowing the aggregate macroeconomy.
Valuation output!B18.economic_intuition: A firm cannot grow faster than the economy in perpetuity without becoming the economy itself. Constraining g to the risk-free rate (4.90%) enforces macroeconomic consistency.

Valuation output!B21.label: Sum of Present Values (Going Concern EV)
Valuation output!B21.methodology: Combines the present value of the 10-year discrete free cash flows ($421.7B) and the present value of the terminal value ($1,388.7B) to determine total unadjusted going-concern enterprise value.
Valuation output!B21.economic_intuition: This reflects the intrinsic enterprise value of Anthropic under the sole assumption that it survives as a going concern in perpetuity without failure or distress liquidation.

Valuation output!B22.label: Probability of Failure
Valuation output!B22.methodology: Anchored to the 10-year cumulative historical default probability for BB-rated corporate bonds from S&P and Moody's credit grids (11.78%), adjusted for Anthropic's multi-year cash cushion. Damodaran selects 10.0%.
Valuation output!B22.economic_intuition: Default risk in money-losing growth companies must be severed from the going-concern WACC. A discount rate assumes infinite survival. Mortality risk is explicitly modeled as a discrete probability of distress.

Valuation output!B23.label: Proceeds if Firm Fails (Distress Salvage)
Valuation output!B23.methodology: Estimates the recovery proceeds realized in distress liquidation as 50% of going-concern enterprise value ($905.2B). Reflects salvage value of proprietary model weights, software IP, trained checkpoints, and customer accounts in a fire-sale.
Valuation output!B23.economic_intuition: Even if Anthropic defaults on hardware commitments, its intellectual property, enterprise customer base, and Claude code retain substantial asset value for acquirers (e.g. hyperscalers).

Valuation output!B24.label: Value of Operating Assets (Distress-Adjusted EV)
Valuation output!B24.methodology: Weighting going-concern value (90%) and distress liquidation proceeds (10%). Equation: Operating Assets = Sum of PV * (1 - P_fail) + P_fail * Proceeds. Takes an explicit $90.5B haircut (-5.3%) off operating assets.
Valuation output!B24.economic_intuition: This is Damodaran's signature mechanism for pricing mortality risk without artificially distorting the cost of capital.

Valuation output!B25.label: Total Debt (Reported + Capitalized Compute)
Valuation output!B25.methodology: Combines reported balance sheet debt ($109,316M) with the present value of non-cancelable compute and operating lease commitments ($376,003.8M).
Valuation output!B25.economic_intuition: Anthropic's massive minimum commitments to AWS and GCP for GPU clusters have binding contractual standing. Treating them as operating expenses understates financial leverage and overstates operating margins.

Valuation output!B27.label: Cash and Cash Equivalents
Valuation output!B27.methodology: Adds existing balance sheet cash and short-term liquid investments ($112,389M).
Valuation output!B27.economic_intuition: Cash represents non-operating assets that must be added back to enterprise value to transition from operating assets to equity value. Anthropic's $112B cash provides an immediate 2-year liquidity runway.

Valuation output!B28.label: Expected Net IPO Proceeds
Valuation output!B28.methodology: Adds anticipated primary capital raised in the public offering ($100,000M).
Valuation output!B28.economic_intuition: Primary capital infusions increase firm equity and cash balances dollar-for-dollar. When combined with existing cash, Anthropic will possess over $212B in liquid reserves.

Valuation output!B30.label: Total Value of Equity
Valuation output!B30.methodology: Standard Corporate Finance equity bridge: Equity = Operating Assets - Debt - Minority Interest + Cash + IPO Proceeds + Non-Operating Assets.
Valuation output!B30.economic_intuition: Calculates the total intrinsic equity value across all outstanding share classes before deducting employee option dilution overhang.

Valuation output!B31.label: Value of Employee Options Overhang
Valuation output!B31.methodology: Evaluates granted employee stock options using the Black-Scholes option pricing model ($472.3M) rather than arbitrary treasury stock exercise methods.
Valuation output!B31.economic_intuition: Deducting option value from total equity separates the equity claim of option holders from common stockholders, preventing dilution double-counting.

Valuation output!B32.label: Value of Equity in Common Stock
Valuation output!B32.methodology: Total Equity ($1,450,950.8M) minus Option Value ($472.3M) = $1,450,478.5M ($1.450 Trillion).
Valuation output!B32.economic_intuition: The net residual value that directly belongs to public common equity investors.

Valuation output!B33.label: Diluted Shares Outstanding
Valuation output!B33.methodology: Combines base common shares on the balance sheet with unvested restricted stock units (RSUs) to establish diluted share count of 3,302.267 Million shares.
Valuation output!B33.economic_intuition: Using diluted share count ensures that all equity claims are appropriately shared across public and insider ownership.

Valuation output!B34.label: Estimated Intrinsic Value Per Share
Valuation output!B34.methodology: Common Equity Value ($1,450,478.5M) divided by 3,302.267M shares = $439.24 per share.
Valuation output!B34.economic_intuition: The final intrinsic target fair value per share from Damodaran's 10-year Ginzu DCF model following the Q3 2026 leaked numbers update.

Valuation output!B35.label: Rumored IPO Offering Price
Valuation output!B35.methodology: The rumored target offering price per share ($525.00) based on leaked investment banking roadshow previews.
Valuation output!B35.economic_intuition: Implies a target market cap of $1.734 Trillion.

Valuation output!B36.label: Price as % of Intrinsic Value
Valuation output!B36.economic_intuition: Anthropic is priced at a 19.53% premium over Damodaran's intrinsic fair value (-16.33% downside). Investors paying $525 are pricing in even higher growth or zero failure risk.

Operating lease converter!C28.label: Debt Value of Compute & Leases
Operating lease converter!C28.methodology: Sums the discounted present values of nominal contractual compute cluster commitments across Years 1 through 6+ ($468,232M nominal) discounted at 6.2828% pre-tax cost of debt.
Operating lease converter!C28.economic_intuition: These commitments are legally binding contractual obligations for GPU hardware. Capitalizing them turns operating commitments into $376.0B of synthetic debt on the balance sheet.

Operating lease converter!C15.label: Pre-tax Cost of Debt for Leases
Operating lease converter!C15.methodology: Risk-free rate (4.94%) + BB+ synthetic rating default spread (1.34%) = 6.2828%.
Operating lease converter!C15.economic_intuition: The discount rate used to capitalize operating leases must reflect the company's pre-tax borrowing cost for secured/unsecured term debt.

Operating lease converter!F31.label: Depreciation on Operating Lease Asset
Operating lease converter!F31.methodology: Calculates annual straight-line depreciation on the synthetic compute asset ($53,714.8M).
Operating lease converter!F31.economic_intuition: Once leases are capitalized, the full lease payment is replaced on the income statement by depreciation of the asset and interest on the synthetic debt.

Operating lease converter!F32.label: Adjustment to Operating Earnings (Leases)
Operating lease converter!F32.methodology: Current year lease expense ($52M) minus depreciation ($53,714.8M) = -$53,662.8M adjustment to pre-tax operating earnings.
Operating lease converter!F32.economic_intuition: Capitalizing massive future compute commitments front-loads depreciation charges, significantly restating base-year operating income.

R& D converter!D24.label: Value of Capitalized Research Asset
R& D converter!D24.methodology: Sums the unamortized portions of current and past 3 years R&D expenditures ($16,979M current at 100%, $12,645M Yr -1 at 66.7%, $3,366M Yr -2 at 33.3%) to create a $26,531M research asset.
R& D converter!D24.economic_intuition: In GAAP/IFRS, R&D is expensed immediately. Damodaran treats R&D as capital investment, recognizing an amortizable intangible asset that creates multi-year cash-flow generating power.
dependents: Input sheet!B14 (Restated Book Value of Equity)

R& D converter!E24.label: Amortization of Research Asset
R& D converter!E24.methodology: Calculates current-year amortization expense across historical R&D tranches ($5,534.3M).
R& D converter!E24.economic_intuition: Replaces expensed R&D with economic amortization. Since current R&D ($16,979M) exceeds amortization ($5,534M), base operating income is boosted by +$11,444.7M.

Cost of capital worksheet!B13.label: Cost of Capital (WACC)
Cost of capital worksheet!B13.methodology: Blended weighted average cost of capital: Cost of Equity (10.05%) * 94.7% weight + After-tax Cost of Debt (4.70%) * 5.3% weight = 9.74%.
Cost of capital worksheet!B13.economic_intuition: Represents the opportunity cost of capital for investing in Anthropic. Sits near the 90th percentile of US tech firms and transitions to 9.13% terminal.

Cost of capital worksheet!B23.label: Unlevered Pure-Play Business Beta
Cost of capital worksheet!B23.methodology: Average unlevered beta for US Software (System & Application) industry, eliminating the distortion of individual company regression noise.
Cost of capital worksheet!B23.economic_intuition: Measures the pure operating risk of Anthropic's enterprise software business without leverage.

Cost of capital worksheet!B24.label: Macro Risk-Free Rate (Rf)
